newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mediation breaks down in Tsumeb mine strike.
newsitem.headline: Mediation breaks down in Tsumeb mine strike.

text.p: Mediation efforts to end a five-week-old strike at Tsumeb Corp Ltd (TCL) in Namibia broke down on Thursday, owners Gold Fields Namibia Ltd said.
"The company agreed that the mediation should end at this point in time," Gold Fields Namibia said in a statement.
"Mediation has been terminated. The strike has not been resolved," a company spokesman told Reuters from Nambia.
The company said that despite the mediation breakdown between management and the Mineworkers' Union of Namibia (MUN), it remained positive the strike would be resolved soon.
The company said it planned to put forward a proposal next week and, if the union accepted it, negotiations could resume within the context of mediation or directly with management.
Tsumeb mines and smelters have been shut down since August 23 when MUN members went on strike over pay.
The company said last week the Tsumeb mine was flooding. Pumping at the two other mines of Kombat and Otjihase was satisfactory.
TCL has started repairs on the copper smelter, damaged by strikers at the start of the dispute. The work is expected to take until early November.
The strike is costing TCL some 80 tonnes a day in lost copper production and a similar amount in lost lead.
The lead smelter appears undamaged, but will still take around two weeks to restart.

TCL produced just under 30,000 tonnes of blister copper last year and 27,000 tonnes of lead. Most of the lead was produced from bought-in material while copper output was from TCL mines. --Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
